# The dist builds regenerate an app page that links a manifest they never copy

## The defect

An app that ships a `manifest.webmanifest` next to its `index.html` (linked as `<link rel="manifest" href="./manifest.webmanifest">`) loses it in every built environment. The webpack app build (`buildScripts/webpack`) regenerates `dist/<env>/apps/<app>/index.html` — manifest link included — but copies nothing next to it; the esm build (`buildScripts/build/esmodules.mjs`) copies only `.mjs`/`.json`/`.html` plus `/resources/`, so `.webmanifest` falls through there too. Result: every bundled page fetches its own manifest and logs a 404 pair on boot (`Manifest fetch … failed, code 404`). `grep -rn webmanifest buildScripts/` returns nothing — the extension is handled nowhere.

Witnessed live in a private consumer workspace on current `dev` (both webpack envs and dist/esm); reproducible in any workspace by adding a manifest to a generated app. The engine's own apps mostly ship without manifests, which is why the gap has stayed invisible.

The dist tree must stay self-contained (the deployment story serves it as its own root), so the fix is copying the asset into the dist app folder — not rewriting the link to reach back into the source tree.

One adjacent inconsistency worth settling in the same pass: the webpack build lowercases the dist app folder (`apps/myapp`) while the esm build keeps the source casing (`apps/myApp`). On a case-sensitive filesystem those are two different URL namespaces for the same app; a copy step has to case-match today instead of joining paths.

### The one statement this ledger does NOT certify

That the *previous* fold would `ENOENT` on a case-sensitive filesystem is a **source read**, not a measured claim — no case-sensitive host was exercised. It is recorded as the motivation, and it is not evidence.

### AC-4 — DELIVERED, browser-witnessed

**Superseding this section's previous text, which said AC-4 was unmet and owned here.** That was accurate when written and the witness has since been run, so the operative body should not go on declaring an open bound that is closed.

Real headless Chrome boots the generated built page at PR #17933's exact head. A camelCase fixture app (`apps/manifestProbe`, carrying `manifest.webmanifest`) is built by the real webpack dev app build, then booted under the repository's own e2e Playwright config — which brings its own dev server rooted at the project directory. **Chrome resolves the `<link rel="manifest">` itself** via `Page.getAppManifest`; the test never supplies the URL. Manifest body delivered, zero manifest-related console errors, with a red control against the copied artifact alone (green → red → green).

One finding from that run worth keeping, because it would have made a naive assertion silently vacuous: **`page.on('response')` never fires for the manifest.** Chrome issues that fetch from the browser process, not as a renderer resource load — so `getAppManifest.data` is the fetch receipt, and a network-event assertion would have observed nothing while appearing to pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] After a webpack env build, `dist/<env>/apps/<app>/` contains the app's `manifest.webmanifest` whenever the source app has one; a spec pins it.
- [x] The esm build's copy set includes `.webmanifest` (or the shared copy step covers it).
- [x] The dist app-folder casing is consistent across the webpack and esm builds, or the divergence is documented where the builds define it.
- [x] A built app page with a manifest boots with zero manifest-fetch console errors (headless probe).

### Residual, and it is not owned by this ticket

**AC-4 is HTTP-probed, not browser-witnessed.** The manifest fetch was resolved over HTTP from the built tree exactly as a browser would resolve the link — but no browser was booted, so nothing here can see a fetch the page never issues, a manifest the parser rejects, or a console error. PR #17933's Post-Merge Validation now carries that as owed work under **#17931** (*"a dist/esm workspace fixture proves imports resolve, but never boots the app"* — the same gap one layer along), which survives this ticket's close.

An earlier revision of that PR body claimed *"Every AC is verified"* while its own Evidence line said no browser was booted. Both could not be true; the Evidence line was the honest one, and the contradiction is corrected there.

- 2026-08-31T12:38:36Z @tobiu referenced in commit `e7cd7b6` - "fix(build): carry an app page's static siblings into the dist tree (#17923) (#17933)

The webpack app builds enumerate only the three files they generate and the esm
build gates its walk on .mjs/.json/.html plus /resources/, so a root-level
manifest.webmanifest fell through both and every built page 404'd on boot.

The extension set now lives in one place all three call sites read, because the
two copy sets drifting apart is the defect itself, not an instance of it.

Also stops folding an app folder to lower case. The fold was applied to the read
path as well as the write, and copyResources already used the true casing, so the
webpack output diverged from both the source tree and the esm build. Only the
synthetic Docs key keeps the fold. Verified a no-op for all 14 engine apps, which
are already lower case."

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-08-31T13:06:45Z

## Post-merge consumer receipt — and one caveat consumers need before they believe their own eyes

@neo-opus-vega ran this against a real consumer workspace after the merge. Both halves verified:

- **The manifest copy works in both webpack envs.** The consumer **retired its local manifest-copy shim** — the builds now emit them, confirmed post-clean-rebuild.
- **The casing lands as source-cased folders.**

### The caveat, and it is the load-bearing one

**On a clean build.** Stale lowercase `dist/<env>/apps/*` directories from before this change **mask the fix via APFS case-folding** — the filesystem happily resolves `dist/development/apps/myapp` and `.../myApp` to the same directory, so a consumer building over an existing tree sees the old casing and concludes nothing changed.

**Consumers must clean `dist/<env>/apps` once.** Until they do, the correct behaviour is invisible on macOS.

That is worth stating plainly because it inverts the usual debugging instinct: the build is right and the *filesystem* is lying, so more rebuilding without cleaning produces more of the same wrong answer. It is also why a case-sensitive host would have shown this immediately — the same asymmetry this ticket's own "would `ENOENT` on a case-sensitive filesystem" note describes, which remains a source read rather than a measurement.
